title: Optimized protocol for the generation of an orthotopic colon cancer mouse model and metastasis
protocol: Remove cell culture medium by aspiration using a 2 mL pipette.
Wash cells with 5 mL of room temperature PBS.
Add 3 mL of Tryplee Express to a T75 cm² flask for detaching cells.
Incubate cells at 37°C until they detach, approximately 3-5 minutes depending on cell type.
Add 15 mL of culture media containing 10% FBS to inactivate Tryplee Express.
Take 10 μL of cell suspension and add 10 μL of trypan blue for counting cells.
Count cells using a cell counter.
Calculate the volume needed to obtain 0.5 × 10⁶ cells in 100 μL per mouse.
Spin down cells for 3 minutes at 231 g.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend cells in 100 μL of a solution made of 50:50 culture medium (DMEM without FBS) and Matrigel on ice.
Keep cells on ice until injection into mice.
Detach Matrigel drops by scratching using the tip of a 1 mL pipette.
Aspirate the drop and medium using a 1 mL pipette.
Transfer all drops to a 15 mL tube.
Add medium until 10 mL to balance the centrifuge.
Spin down cells for 10 min at 450 g at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant.
Add 1 mL of room temperature Tryplee Express to the pellet.
Incubate for 3 min at 37°C, 5% CO2.
Assess under the cell culture microscope that tumoroids are dissociated into single cells or small clusters.
Add 5 mL medium to inactivate Tryplee Express.
Take 10 μL of cell suspension and add 10 μL of trypan blue.
Deposit this mix on cell counting chamber slides.
Count cells with cell counter.
Calculate the volume of cells needed to obtain 0.5 × 10^6 cells in 100 μL that will be injected in each mouse.
Spin down cells for 10 min at 450 g at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend cells in 100 μL of a solution made of 50:50 culture medium (DMEM/F12 without FBS) and Matrigel on ice to prevent premature polymerization of Matrigel.
Keep cells on ice until injection into mice.
Anesthetize the mouse with 3% isoflurane and an airflow of 2 L per minute until it falls asleep.
Reduce isoflurane to 2% with an airflow of 0.5 L per minute once the mouse is sleeping.
Place tear gel on the eyes of the mice to prevent drying.
Inject 5 mg/kg Carprofen (Rimadyl) analgesic diluted in PBS subcutaneously.
Position the mouse on its back with hind legs apart, immobilized with surgical tape.
Remove feces present in the colon by gently massaging the mouse’s abdomen.
Pre-heat 0.5 M EDTA, pH8 at 50°C in a water bath for 15 minutes before starting the experiment.
Immerse an interdental brush in the pre-heated EDTA solution for 30 seconds.
Gently insert the interdental brush into the mouse’s anus and advance it 1.5 cm into the colon.
Turn on the vibration of the interdental brush for 10 seconds.
Evaluate the efficiency of crypt removal: Pipette 10 μL of PBS containing crypts on a slide.
Count detached crypts under a cell culture microscope.
Multiply this number by 150 to obtain the total number of detached crypts (that are in 1.5 mL PBS).
If there are no or not enough detached crypts, additional abrasions should be performed, assessing the presence of crypts after each abrasion.
Eliminate the residual EDTA by massaging the mouse’s abdomen for 2 min.
Mix the cell solution gently to avoid bubbles.
Inject cells in the colonic lumen in the area of the lesions made with the interdental brush.
Pipette 100 μL of a solution containing cells and Matrigel using a 200 μL pipette tip.
Insert the pipette tip very gently into the colonic lumen parallel to the colon wall and advance as far as possible (about 1.5 cm).
Pinch the anus and tip of the pipette with tweezers and slowly pipette out cells into the colonic lumen.
Gently remove the pipette tip while continuing to apply pressure to the clamp to keep the anus closed.
Carefully remove any cone from the anus while maintaining pressure.
Add a drop of surgical glue to close the anus of the mouse.
Hold the mouse in a position with the raised legs and pelvis until it wakes up.
After 4 hours, verify that the anus of the mice is opened.
If not, remove the remaining glue with a damp tissue.
Depose cells as far as possible in the colon without piercing it.
Ensure deposited glue holds the anus closed for at least 4 hours but is self-removed within 4 hours.
Visualize tumor growth by endoscopy from day 7 to day 90.
Anesthetize mice using 3% isoflurane, 2 L per minute until they fall asleep.
Reduce isoflurane concentration to 2%, maintaining airflow of 0.5 L per minute during imaging.
Immobilize the mouse with tape on the hind legs.
Remove feces by abdominal massage.
Apply vaseline around the anus.
Gently insert the endoscope into the anus while dilating the colon with air using a 50 ml syringe, typically injecting about 5 ml of air.
Move the endoscope gently throughout the colon while recording the movie.
Place the mouse on its back and administer isoflurane anesthesia before IVIS imaging.
Inject luciferin into the mouse prior to placing it in the imaging chamber of the IVIS system.
Image the mouse using IVIS starting one week after transplantation, once weekly up to 3 months, depending on tumor growth.
Inject 200 μL of a 15 mg/mL luciferin solution intraperitoneally.
Wait 15 min before imaging using IVIS.
Anesthetize the mouse with 3% isoflurane and 2 L per minute air flow until it falls asleep.
Reduce isoflurane to 2% with an airflow of 0.5 L per minute once the mouse is sleeping.
Position the mouse on its back in Xenogen Vivovision IVIS lumina II heating chamber.
Set up exposure time to 1 min, f-stop to 1 and large pixel binning using Living Image software.
Maintain the mouse’s body temperature at a constant stage temperature of 37°C.
Sacrifice mice by cervical dislocation.
Open the abdomen and inspect organs (liver, lungs, peritoneum) for macroscopic metastases.
Cut the urogenital system and pelvis.
Excise the anus and the distal part of the colon.
Inspect the colon for the presence of tumors.
Fix organs in 25 mL of 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) dissolved in PBS using a 50 mL tube at 4°C with gentle shaking for 1 hour.
Decant PFA and wash tissues with PBS for 10 minutes at 4°C with gentle shaking.
Replace PBS with 15 mL of 15% sucrose in a 50 mL tube at 4°C with gentle shaking.
Incubate tissue in 15% sucrose for 2 hours at 4°C.
Decant solution and replace it with 15 mL of 30% sucrose in a 50 mL tube.
Incubate tissue in 30% sucrose for 2 hours at 4°C.
Place tissue in plastic 15 × 15 × 5 mm mold and include in OCT at room temperature.
Orient the colon vertically (lumen of the colon facing up) with the anus sitting at the bottom of the mold.
Place the mold at -20°C for at least 2 h to let OCT solidify.
Trim the OCT block until reaching the tissue, focusing on the anus and rectum until reaching the tumor that can be seen macroscopically.
Cut colon/tumor into 8 to 10 μm-thick slices.
Transfer the tissue to Super frost + slides by contact.
Add 500 μL of a solution containing 25 μg/mL DAPI in PBS to the sections.
Incubate for 30 min at room temperature.
Remove the DAPI solution and add 8 drops of Aquapolymount mounting solution on the tissue section.
Cover with 24 × 50 mm coverslip.
Leave to dry for at least 1 h before imaging.
Image samples using an epifluorescent microscope or, for higher resolution images, a confocal microscope.
